text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Friday.

GERMANY - Bunds spent much of Friday clawing back some of Thursday's 1.5 point loss in what traders said was largely thin trade ahead of the weekend. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.76, up 0.37 from Thursday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK gilt futures ended higher, clawing back some of the ground lost in recent weeks, but below their intraday high. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 108-20/32, up 07/32 from Thursday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures recovered from an early selloff as a more positive tone returned to the German and U.S. bond markets and domestic investors snapped up bonds at the lows, traders said. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 127.90 down 0.04 from Thursday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt markets held the day's gains of around 60 basis points as dealers squared books going into a long weekend in Italy. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 127.95 up 0.65 from Thursday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - US Treasury market remained narrowly range-bound at midmorning. U.S. November construction spending rose 1.9 percent. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 111-30/32, up 18/32 from Thursday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.7 percent.

JAPAN - The Japanese bond market was closed for a National Holiday. In after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 123.90, down 0.31 from Thursday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market ended the first few days of 1997 on a quiet note, but activity was expected to increase next week. The traditional January rush of deals could be slightly delayed by further holidays in Europe, including Germany, Italy and Spain, on Monday, dealers said.
There were few firm details available of upcoming deals, with plans not expected to be finalised until players were back at their desks.
"Both issuers and lead managers expect activity in all areas next week," a syndicate manager at a British bank said.
